heading: client/manifest.json, field by field
body: The manifest is a standard web app manifest. A browser reads its standard members to install the application. Tachyon reads some of the same members for a native build. It also adds one member of its own, tac, and a browser ignores it. tac holds the public configuration that services bind, and Tachyon's own settings: the application identity and window, shared scripts and styles, service-worker cache rules, page metadata, the sitemap (ADR 0052) and the browser API grants in `browserApis` (ADR 0065). The whole file is public, because the build publishes it at /manifest.webmanifest. Do not put anything private in it. A web build reads the tac settings it needs: scripts, styles, cache rules, metadata, the origin, the sitemap and `browserApis`. `browserApis` lists the browser APIs that need the user's consent and that the services may use: any of `clipboard`, `share`, `notifications` and `geolocation`, each once, for example `"browserApis": ["clipboard", "geolocation"]`. Any other name stops the build (`TY1601`). The page refuses an API that is not listed. A native build takes its name, entry route, identifier, version and window from this file only. There is no tac.config.js and no tachyon.json: a build refuses both and says where each value moved. Eight `check` settings turn one build rule off while you migrate, for Tac code only: `tac.cohesion.check`, `tac.duplication.check`, `tac.dependencies.check`, `tac.names.check`, `tac.signatures.check`, `tac.constants.check`, `tac.visibility.check` and `tac.types.check`, each `false` (`tac.types.check` is off until you set it to `true`; see Cohesive services, Utilities, Dependencies point down, Plain-English names, Small signatures, Named values, Public only when used and Types in every language). `tac.accessibility.check: false` turns off the accessible-view check (`TY1336`, see Templates). `tac.budgets.script` and `tac.budgets.webassembly` set the size budget of every route in kilobytes (defaults 200 and 3584), and `tac.budgets.check: false` turns that check off (`TY1337`, see Build and deploy). `tac.simplify.suggest` set to `false` hides the simpler-form suggestions for Tac code (see Simpler forms). `tac.names.words` lists words of your domain, such as a product name, that Tac names may use. `tac.go.compiler` chooses the Go compiler for Go web services: `"tinygo"` or `"go"`; without it a release build tries TinyGo first and falls back to Go (see WebAssembly compilers per language). `tac.dotnet.aot: true` compiles C# and F# web services ahead of time in a release build: faster for heavy computing, but a larger download.
